A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and supplementary Sections 6–10 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–2, generated-image comparisons, and appendix validation of simulated camera effects.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a training-dataset-size experiment for shutter-speed control in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Contrastive Camera Learning is renamed Differential Camera Intrinsics Learning. Sections 3 and 8 retain the same dimensionality lifting, simulated training data, coarse embeddings, adjacent CLIP-feature differences, encoder integration and AnimateDiff adaptation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate bokeh rendering, focal length, shutter speed and color temperature using the same described photographic and public-image sources. The added dataset-size experiment varies sample counts within the existing shutter-speed task.

E2.justification: The four-task comparisons retain SD3, FLUX, and AnimateDiff and CameraCtrl with and without fine-tuning. SD3 and FLUX remain evaluated baselines despite the omission of their CLIP scores from Table 1.

E3.justification: Figure 6 introduces a shutter-speed experiment varying training-set size up to 5,000 samples. Existing experiments retain 1,000 images per task, 75 test-setting sets, the same training configuration and the same metric calculations; CLIP is only relabeled.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a dataset-size sensitivity study for shutter-speed control. The encoder-difference, continuous-versus-discrete sampling and frame-count ablations remain, as does the appendix comparison of simulated and optical zoom.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added scaling plot contains point estimates without error bars, and the fixed-seed illustration in Figure 2 is retained.

E6.justification: New Figure 6 reports a nonmonotonic scaling curve, peaking near 0.94 accuracy at approximately 1,500 samples. Table 1 replaces all eight SD3/FLUX CLIP scores with dashes, including bokeh scores 0.3278 and 0.3257. All remaining numerical entries in Tables 1–2 match v1; the appendix comparison images are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix Equations 1–7 retain the same field-of-view formulas, imaging model, assumptions and piecewise color-temperature conversion. No substantive mathematical derivation, definition or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: scene-consistent control of camera intrinsics through dimensionality lifting and the renamed camera-learning approach. The claimed scope and principal advantages remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new scaling experiment as evidence that roughly 1,000 samples suffice for efficient learning of camera physics. It also narrows the interpretation of CLIP from general generation quality to prompt following. Existing focal-length limitations and computational tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract explicitly states that code is available through the existing project page; v1 identifies that page and its visual results without explicitly advertising code availability. Training, hardware, simulation and encoder implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Fang et al., Camera settings as tokens: Modeling photography on latent diffusion models, when discussing camera-intrinsic control and missing multi-setting metadata. The broader related-work discussion and positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract and introduction, reorders introductory explanations, converts several lists to prose and replaces contrastive terminology throughout. The overall section organization and most method and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds scaling Figure 6, relocates Figure 3, updates diagram labels and table headers/highlighting, and adds a supplementary title heading. Appendix figures are renumbered, and the final figure caption correctly identifies color-temperature control instead of focal-length control.

improvement.justification: The new scaling ablation provides limited additional support for data efficiency, and describing CLIP as prompt following improves precision. However, Table 1 removes all SD3/FLUX CLIP scores without explanation while retaining comparative prompt-following claims. With the core camera-control evidence unchanged, the added validation and reduced comparison transparency leave the net quality direction uncertain.
